results.content:
Dreamwork is a job search agent that does the applying for you. Most job seekers send applications into a void: dozens of forms, no replies, no idea what went wrong. Dreamwork was built to end that. Upload your resume and the agent reads what you have actually done, then searches millions of live job listings for roles where your experience genuinely fits. Listings come from company career sites and major job boards, with thousands of new roles arriving every day. For each match, Dreamwork explains why you fit, so you can judge the role yourself instead of trusting a black-box score. When you are ready to apply, Dreamwork prepares the whole application: a resume tailored to the role, a cover letter grounded in your real experience, and answers to the employer's questions, all built from [...] and answers to the employer's questions, all built from what your resume already shows, never invented. Apply one role at a time, or turn on auto-apply and let the agent keep working while you get on with your life. Replies, interviews, and offers land in one pipeline, so you always know where every application stands and what to do next. Matching and tailoring are free, and on the free plan you can apply yourself using the employer’s own application link. Pro adds sending applications for you, at $33 a month billed quarterly ($99 every 3 months) or $39 month to month, with a 7-day free Pro trial. Not affiliated with DreamWorks Animation. results.title: AI Job Search Agent: Your Search, Run for You | Dreamwork
results.content:
### Bot

A form-filler with a quota: one resume, blasted at everything with a submit button. Fast, easy to detect, and the reason recruiters distrust automation.

### Agent

Owns the loop: finds live roles that fit, tailors real materials for each, applies when you tap Apply or on Autopilot, and tracks every reply. You supervise; it executes.

## What the agent does while you're doing something else

A job search has a dozen recurring chores. This is the loop Dreamwork keeps running:

1. ### Watches the market

   Dreamwork crawls company career sites daily, so matches come from listings that are actually live — the same corpus behindour public hiring research.
2. ### Ranks what's worth your time [...] Yes — this is where Dreamwork is different. We expose an MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint, so an agent you already use, like Claude, can search Dreamwork's live roles, generate application packs, check your pipeline, and apply, all with the same approval guardrails. Your agent brings the reasoning; Dreamwork brings live jobs and the ability to act.

### How much does an AI job search agent cost?

Dreamwork is free to start: ranked matches from live listings, and a tailored resume and cover letter for 5 jobs a day to apply with on the employer's site. Autopilot, where the agent applies to your top matches for you, and the recruiter-reply inbox are part of Pro. You can judge the agent's matching on the free tier before paying anything.

### Does Dreamwork give refunds? [...] New roles are scored against your resume as they appear. No sponsored placements — the ranking is the fit.
3. ### Prepares every application

   For roles you add, the agent writes a tailored resume, cover letter, and custom answers in about 20 seconds, from your real experience.
4. ### Applies, one tap or on Autopilot

   Review and send each pack yourself, or on Pro, turn on Autopilot and let the agent apply to your strongest matches above the score you set. Pause it anytime.
5. ### Keeps score honestly

   Pipeline status per role, recruiter replies routed to one inbox, nothing lost in email. You always know where the search stands.

results.title: Show HN: Dreamwork – a job search site I made after Indeed fired my pregnant wif | Hacker News
results.content:
It is now useful enough that I think strangers can try it and find serious value.

What it does today:

- indexes ~100k curated tech jobs

- tries to avoid stale/duplicate aggregator garbage

- uses semantic matching instead of only keyword search

- generates an “application pack” for each job: tailored resume, cover letter, and answers to common/custom questions

- lets the user edit everything before applying

- helps keep track of saved jobs and generated materials

Auto apply is the part I’m conflicted about. I do t think blindly spraying applications is good for the candidates (chance of hiring is already low, even with hard work and customization), recruiters (they’re swamped), or the world (we don’t need more slop).
